method: Independent Astra bounded read of retained native image; Root synthesis; no native execution or code changes.
finding: Normal native login writes account configuration and credentials separately. Native siblings watch shared configuration; credential-only adoption evidence does not exercise this complete path.
contracts: The login profile path writes native account/organization, billing/seat/onboarding fields and fresh profileFetchedAt. Credentials persist separately through a refresh-lock wrapper with conditional unlocked/fallback paths.
Native global config writes take configPath.lock, reread and merge. Credential and config writes are not one atomic transaction; config writer fallback paths exist.
The normal config watcher polls at one-second intervals (or an optional native watcher), accepts newer mtime, defers local pending writes and installs parsed config into cache.
Request account metadata reads oauthAccount through the shared config cache, so common config reload is a plausible sibling propagation mechanism.
The healthy sibling auth recheck returns without broad reauthentication unless auth state is missing or invalid. Config reload alone does not prove the full local-login invalidation path.
Local native login clears additional provider/model/tool caches and can cancel an armed quota episode as account_switch; sibling equivalence was not established.
next_native_question: Does a healthy sibling sharing genuinely native-written B configuration adopt B request identity and relevant policy state, and what happens to active, idle, permission and quota waits?
limits: No live/synthetic native execution in this source study.
